The greedy Ringside Pass is such a negative that it overshadows the positives in the game. The progression for the Ringside Pass is a ridiculous slog, and sucks the fun out of the game. 2K and WWE should be embarrassed with what they have done. But I guess we shouldn't be that surprised given how greedy and selfish WWE has become with their TV and live events. Disappointing steaming pile of abusive waste.

Update: MyRise is boring and tedious... and guess what? You get to do it twice to unlock stuff you already paid for. And then there is the punishing showcase where you get to play color by numbers and follow inane prompts. What a boring, frustrating slog. Once again to unlock stuff that should have already been unlocked.

The island is alright I guess. Some of the quests overstay their welcome and the Tower is fundamentally uninspired. Oh, and the prices for all the cosmetics unlocks is unreal given the slow trickle of currency the game provides. All to make you so miserable that you will be tempted to spend real money to avoid playing anymore of their terrible game.

But this game killed my future purchases for the franchise because I know the developers wont optimize the game to run on pc. Only if Sony was not on garbage, I would have just bought it on console and kept playing it on there. I dont recommend playing any sports game on PC. Just buy a copy on console.

WWE 2K26 builds on what made last year's game so good.
This year's game is tremendously fun, engaging and likely my favorite wrestling game to date.

The ragdoll physics add great new moments in matches that just couldn't happen in the past games.

The season pass is a bit of a let down, while I don't have a problem grinding the game, I like playing it, having to do so for content you already paid nearly $200 for starts to wear on my patience. The monetization for the series will likely continue to get much worse, but the gameplay itself is the best its ever been.

I have been a fan of this series for years, but WWE 2k26 is where I draw the line. There practices have felt scummy and like a scam. The day one patch didn't address the many bugs, instead it made it harder to earn experience to unlock the tiers, trying to force people to purchase tier skips. They are so heavily focused on micro transactions instead making a great game. At this point I am done with 2k games. I hate giving bad reviews, but 2k is predatory. Their actions should have consequences. They will never get money from me again.

Garbage DLC implementation that makes you 'earn' characters advertised as 'included' in any version you can purchase, BS 'card collecting' and lootbox modes that make these practices even more egregious, and drop-out level social media marketing managers that view all of these predictable complaints as personal attacks.

You can't start the game without creating a 2k account, the ui is horrendous, and gameplay is exactly the same as previous entries: warts, crashes, stutters and all. Even the 'most expansive roster ever' claim is an outright misrepresentation of what's actually being offered here, because NOW every copy & paste instance of a wrestler in a new outfit (or hat) is counted as a completely new & different character.

This entire package is pathetic, borderline illegal, and I will not purchase another 2K game until everyone having anything to do with this one has been fired, publicly humiliated and banned from game development in general.

Since that's unlikely to happen in any way that i would notice, I'll close by simply saying that I will miss 2K games every bit as much as I miss Ubisoft's: not at all.

Pros: 

1) Booker T's Commentary

Cons: 

1) The facial animations look like a PS2 game. The mouths barely move when they talk and there are literally no facial expressions. By far the worst mocap/models I have seen in this series to date.

2) The sheer amount of content you're locked out of at the start of the game is borderline criminal. You're paying all this money for 25% of the game at best.

3) Who the hell thought it was a good idea to put a battle pass in a wrestling game? Want to use that cool piece of clothing for your create-a-character? Too bad, you need to reach level 35 of the battle pass to use it. Ridiculous.

Overall: 

It's no surprise to most that 2K games are a shameless cash grab year after year, with little to no changes being made other than the roster, but I think we've finally reached the point where they're actually making the games WORSE, and charging MORE for it. I regret buying this game (even on sale) as I don't believe 2K deserves a single dollar from this. This is a spit in the face of consumers, and I can only hope that this review saves you from making the same mistake I did and stops you from giving these greedy b*stards one single cent of your hard earned money.
